concept_widget.title: The Gaza Raid (28 Feb 1955): From Fedayeen Raids to Nasser’s Arms Pivot
concept_widget.caption: Click each stage to trace how cross-border guerrilla raids and Israel’s Operation Black Arrow humiliated Gamal Abdel Nasser and triggered Egypt’s quest for modern weapons.

items.title: Pan-Arab Leadership & Gaza Fedayeen Sabotage
items.takeaway: Emerging as Egypt’s leader in 1954, Nasser championed Pan-Arab nationalism while allowing Palestinian fedayeen guerrillas to mount armed sabotage raids into southern Israel from Egyptian-held Gaza.

items.title: Operation Black Arrow Strikes the Gaza Garrison
items.takeaway: Authorised by Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion and Defence Minister Moshe Dayan on 28 February 1955, Israeli paratroopers stormed an Egyptian military garrison in Gaza in a major reprisal raid.

items.title: Army Humiliation & Urgent Quest for Modern Arms
items.takeaway: Operation Black Arrow exposed the weakness of Egypt’s armed forces before Nasser’s own officers, convincing him that Egypt could not deter Israel without modern jet fighters, tanks, and heavy artillery.

widgets.expected_heading: Syrian Support for Fatah Border Raids

concept_widget.title: Guerrilla War & Syrian Patronage (1965–1966): Fatah ↔ Damascus Regime ↔ Golan Shelling
concept_widget.caption: Slide or click across the three stages to trace how Yasser Arafat’s Fatah raids and Syrian military backing escalated border tension along the Golan Heights.

stops.label: 1. Yasser Arafat & Fatah’s Revolutionary Strategy (Kuwait – Jan 1965)
stops.summary: Frustrated by conservative Arab diplomacy, younger Palestinian militants led by Yasser Arafat founded Fatah in Kuwait to wage independent guerrilla attacks designed to ignite a wider Arab-Israeli war.

traits.value: First Raid on Israeli Water Canal

stops.label: 2. Radical Military Regime in Damascus Arms Fatah (1966)
stops.summary: After a radical military regime seized power in Damascus in 1966, Syria became Fatah’s primary state sponsor—supplying advanced weaponry, training camps, and safe operational bases.

stops.label: 3. Golan Heights Artillery & Israeli Retaliation Warnings (1966–67)
stops.summary: From fortified bunkers high on the Golan Heights, Syrian artillery routinely shelled Israeli tractors and farming kibbutzim in the Hula Valley below, provoking stern warnings of Israeli military retaliation.

widgets.expected_heading: Soviet Warning, UNEF Expelled & Straits of Tiran Closed

concept_widget.title: 13–22 May 1967: How False Intelligence Triggered the Straits of Tiran Crisis
concept_widget.caption: Click each milestone across the ten-day May 1967 escalation to see how a false Soviet intelligence tip led Nasser to cross Israel’s explicit 1957 red line.

items.title: False Soviet Warning of an Israeli Buildup
items.takeaway: Although UN observers confirmed no Israeli troop buildup existed on Syria’s border, Moscow’s false 13 May warning forced Nasser to act boldly to defend his prestige as champion of Pan-Arabism.

items.title: Egyptian Army Mobilises Across the Sinai Peninsula
items.takeaway: On 14–15 May 1967, Nasser marched 100,000 troops and 1,000 tanks into Sinai, demanding on 16 May that United Nations Emergency Force (UNEF) peacekeepers withdraw.

items.title: U Thant Withdraws UNEF & Sharm el-Sheikh Occupied
items.takeaway: When UN Secretary-General U Thant withdrew UNEF without Security Council debate, the peacekeeping buffer vanished and Egyptian forces occupied Sharm el-Sheikh overlooking the Gulf of Aqaba.

items.title: Nasser Closes the Straits of Tiran to Israeli Shipping
items.takeaway: Closing the Straits of Tiran on 22 May choked off Eilat’s shipping and vital oil tankers, crossing the explicit red line Israel had warned since 1957 would constitute an act of war.

concept_widget.title: State Within a State: Jordanian Authority vs PFLP Militancy (Late 1960s – 6 Sept 1970)
concept_widget.caption: Click each stage of the Dawson’s Field crisis to see how Dr George Habash’s Marxist PFLP challenged both Yasser Arafat and King Hussein’s control over Jordan.

eras.headline: Marxist PFLP Challenges Arafat & Pioneers Hijackings
eras.summary: Dr George Habash’s Marxist PFLP challenged Arafat’s moderate leadership by pioneering international airliner hijackings to publicise the Palestinian struggle and free jailed guerrillas.

eras.headline: Simultaneous Hijacking of Four Western Airliners
eras.summary: PFLP operatives hijacked four Western passenger airliners simultaneously, forcing three aircraft onto Dawson’s Field—a remote desert landing strip inside Jordan—with over 300 civilian hostages.

eras.headline: Airliners Blown Up Before Global Television Cameras
eras.summary: After evacuating over 300 civilian hostages, PFLP militants blew up the empty airliners on world television—humiliating King Hussein and proving armed groups operated beyond Jordanian government control.

concept_widget.title: The War of Attrition (March 1969 – August 1970): Suez Shelling ↔ Deep Raids ↔ Superpower Truce
concept_widget.caption: Slide or click across the three phases to see how Nasser’s grinding Suez Canal campaign escalated toward a dangerous US–Soviet confrontation before the August 1970 ceasefire.

stops.label: 1. Nasser Launches the War of Attrition Along the Suez Canal (March 1969)
stops.summary: In March 1969, President Nasser launched a grinding artillery war along the Suez Canal to inflict casualties on Israel, stop the 1967 ceasefire line becoming permanent, and force superpower intervention.

stops.label: 2. Concrete Bar-Lev Bunkers & Deep Israeli Air Strikes (1969–70)
stops.summary: While Israeli troops endured heavy Egyptian artillery barrages inside reinforced concrete bunkers along the Bar-Lev Line, Israeli jets struck deep inside the Egyptian heartland.

stops.label: 3. Soviet SAMs, Combat Pilots & US-Brokered Ceasefire (August 1970)
stops.summary: When Moscow deployed advanced surface-to-air missiles and Soviet combat pilots to defend Cairo, fear of direct superpower clash drove Egypt and Israel to accept a US-brokered ceasefire in August 1970.

widgets.expected_heading: Arab Boycott & The Assassination of Sadat

concept_widget.title: The Price of Separate Peace (1979–1981): Arab League Boycott & Sadat’s Assassination
concept_widget.caption: Click each stage to trace how Egypt’s bilateral peace treaty with Israel triggered Arab diplomatic isolation, domestic Islamist assassination, and a lasting ‘cold peace’.

items.title: Arab League Expulsion & Sweeping Economic Boycott
items.takeaway: Condemning Sadat for recovering Egyptian territory via a separate treaty, the Arab League suspended Egypt, moved its headquarters from Cairo to Tunis, and imposed sweeping economic boycotts.

items.title: Assassination at the Cairo Victory Parade
items.takeaway: Condemned by domestic Islamist fundamentalists as a traitor to the Islamic cause, Sadat was shot dead on 6 October 1981 by Egyptian Islamic Jihad soldiers while reviewing a Cairo military parade.

items.title: Treaty Preserved & Gradual Arab Reintegration
items.takeaway: Sadat’s successor upheld the formal peace treaty with Israel while steadily repairing Egypt’s severed diplomatic relations with Arab neighbours over the following decade.

concept_widget.title: From UN Recognition to Tunis Exile (1974–1982): PLO Lebanon Raids & Operation Peace for Galilee
concept_widget.caption: Click each milestone from November 1974 to August 1982 to trace how PLO operations in southern Lebanon led to Israel’s siege of Beirut and the PLO’s sea evacuation to Tunis.

items.title: Arafat’s ‘Olive Branch & Gun’ Speech Wins UN Status
items.takeaway: Addressing the UN General Assembly in November 1974, Arafat won official UN observer status and international recognition for Palestinian self-determination.

items.title: ‘Fatahland’ Raids, Operation Litani & UNIFIL
items.takeaway: Ongoing PLO cross-border rocket and guerrilla raids from southern Lebanon (‘Fatahland’) provoked Israel’s 1978 Operation Litani incursion and the deployment of UNIFIL peacekeepers.

items.title: Ariel Sharon Launches Operation Peace for Galilee

metrics.label: Stated Limit
metrics.value: Push PLO 40 km North of Border

items.takeaway: Intended to push PLO forces 40 kilometres north of Israel’s border, Ariel Sharon’s armoured invasion advanced far beyond cabinet limits to lay siege to Beirut for ten weeks.

items.title: US-Mediated Sea Evacuation of 14,000 PLO Fighters
items.takeaway: In August 1982, US mediation ended the Beirut siege by evacuating Yasser Arafat and 14,000 PLO fighters by sea to distant exile in Tunis.

concept_widget.title: Road to Madrid (1989–Oct 1991): How the Soviet Collapse & Gulf War Reshaped Leverage
concept_widget.caption: Click each geopolitical shift from 1989 to October 1991 to see how Washington gained unrivalled Middle East leverage to convene the historic Madrid Peace Conference.

eras.headline: Cold War Patronage Sustains Diplomatic Deadlock
eras.summary: Before 1991, Soviet superpower arms, UN diplomatic vetoes, and financial patronage shielded Arab confrontation states, while Gulf Arab states funded the PLO.

eras.headline: Gulf War Victory, Soviet Collapse & Arafat’s Miscalculation
eras.summary: The 1991 Soviet collapse ended Moscow’s patronage, US Gulf War victory left Washington dominant, and Arafat’s support for Iraq’s Saddam Hussein cost the PLO hundreds of millions in Saudi and Kuwaiti funding.

pillars.status: Lost Gulf Aid; Desperate for Talks

eras.headline: Madrid Peace Conference Breaks 43-Year Taboo
eras.summary: President George H. W. Bush and James Baker brought Israeli, Syrian, Lebanese, and joint Jordanian-Palestinian delegations face to face in Madrid—breaking 43 years of taboos despite PM Yitzhak Shamir’s hardline Likud stance.
